newsitem.title: JAPAN: HSBC Group to expand financial operations in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Group to expand financial operations in Tokyo.

text.p: HSBC Securities Ltd, the capital markets arm of Hong Kong-based HSBC Group, plans to double its staff in Tokyo over the next 18 months, with fellow group member HSBC Midland Bank Plc's Tokyo branch also planning substantial personnel increases, a Midland bank official said.
The staff increases, which have already begun, will see HSBC Securities grow to 50 people from the current 25 in one year to 18 months, Midland Bank Treasurer Chris Pavlou said.
Currency options personnel at Midland will also double to 10, while the bank's foreign exchange staff will increase to roughly 30 from 22, he added.

The expansion will allow the group to strengthen its base in operations such as Japanese government bonds and other fixed-income instruments, as well as increase its emphasis on currency options and Asian currencies, Pavlou said.
Noting that the changes to a large part reflect customers' changing demands, he added: "Our customers are getting more sophisticated, and they need more tools to hedge their risks."
He said the HSBC Group regards the market conditions, such as high costs, that have driven many foreign businesses out of Tokyo in recent years as a great opportunity.

"A lot of other banks are rationalising or moving away... This gives us a chance to go in the front door of a lot of companies where we weren't able to go before," he said, noting the conditions also make it easy to employ quality employees.
Other foreign banks have recently announced an expansion in their Tokyo operations, including French Bank Societie Generale.
The HSBC Group is planning to construct its own 10-storey building in Tokyo's business district, a bank spokeswoman said on Monday.
